decisions.reason: The splash-control target does not alter the separately stated texture, foam consistency, or smooth-mixing requirements.
The conditional splash guard or bowl lip does not determine the whisk-head design, material, or size; the same message's whisk uncertainty is already represented independently.
A splash guard or bowl lip is only a conditional mitigation and does not necessarily change the current bowl capacity, depth, or refill policy.

The candidate already records the same message's distinct pour-flow changes, while prevention of post-close dripping was already present; the mixing-splash modification adds no further pour-state change.
Splash-control requirements do not change the machine's colors or finish.
Splash-control requirements do not change the placard text, position, or viewing orientation.
The source does not change enclosure size or side-profile constraints; a conditional bowl guard does not necessarily alter the enclosure form.
The stronger splash-control target leaves the DJ-turntable visual theme unchanged.
The source preserves the solenoid and states operational pour constraints but does not change the rendered spout's appearance, material, or fabrication method.
The splash-control modification does not change the required wiring-plan deliverable or its detail level.
The source explicitly retains the solenoid approach and does not change the existing button-controlled valve actuation behavior.
A conditional splash guard or bowl lip does not necessarily change the BOM deliverable or sourcing strategy, and the source requests input before finalization rather than mandating a new component.
